The total sum is \(1+2+\cdots+100=5050\). Partition any permutation into 10 disjoint consecutive blocks of length 10. Their sums total 5050, so some block has sum at least \(505\). Hence \(A\ge 505\).

To show no larger \(A\) is guaranteed, pair numbers as \((i,101-i)\). For \(j=1,\dots,10\), form block \(B_j\) from the five pairs with \(i=5j-4,\dots,5j\), ordered as
\[
101-(5j-4),\,5j-4,\,101-(5j-3),\,5j-3,\,\dots,\,101-5j,\,5j.
\]
Each block sums to \(5\cdot 101=505\). For adjacent blocks, the prefix sums satisfy \(P_{j+1}(t)\le P_j(t)\) for \(t=1,\dots,9\). Thus any 10-term window crossing a boundary has sum
\[
505-P_j(t)+P_{j+1}(t)\le 505.
\]
So in this permutation every 10 consecutive terms have sum at most \(505\). Therefore no integer larger than \(505\) is guaranteed.

\[
\boxed{505}
\]
